question.text: The Detailed Public Statement (DPS) must be published within how many working days of the public announcement?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SAST, the Detailed Public Statement (DPS) must be published within 5 working days of the public announcement. The DPS contains comprehensive details about the offer including the offer price, offer size, identity of the acquirer, financial arrangements, and other material terms. Separately, the draft letter of offer is filed with SEBI within 5 working days from the DPS — those two "5 working days" timelines are different. The Trap: 10 working days is the minimum tendering period, not the DPS publication deadline; candidates often swap these timelines. The 5-day window also applies to filing the draft letter of offer (measured from DPS), which is easy to confuse with the DPS publication deadline (measured from the public announcement). Note: Track each leg of the SAST timeline separately — PA, DPS publication (5 working days from PA), draft letter of offer filing with SEBI (5 working days from DPS), and the tendering period — and never collapse the DPS publication and draft letter filing dates.
